facts.claim: The usage-limit text reports spent quota only when the last rate-limit event read was a rejection that names a usage window (five_hour, seven_day, seven_day_opus, seven_day_sonnet, seven_day_overage_included, overage).
facts.catch_criteria: States that the quota mark needs both the usage-limit text and a rejected rate-limit report that names a usage window, and that the text alone is not enough.

facts.claim: A concurrency rejection names no usage window, so no quota mark is recorded; the 429 becomes a rate-limit failure.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the concurrency 429 is classified as a rate limit (throttling), not a spent quota.

facts.claim: The rate-limit failure is retried on the same candidate up to 3 times, waiting the provider's retry delay (capped at 60 s) or a backoff.
facts.catch_criteria: States that the request is retried in place on the same account with a retry delay, and names a bounded retry count.

facts.claim: The failover client's candidate walk owns moving to the next candidate, after the retry budget is spent; the Claude engine adapter only classifies the failure.
facts.catch_criteria: Names the failover client (candidate walk, selectNext) as the owner that advances to another account or provider, not the Claude adapter.

traps.wrong_answer: Any usage-limit text from the engine marks the login's quota spent and suppresses the account.
